tldr: The paper proposes MemSim, a Bayesian simulator using a Bayesian Relation Network (BRNet) and causal generation mechanism to automatically construct reliable, diverse question-answer pairs from simulated user messages for evaluating the memory capability of LLM-based personal assistants.
contributions: Analysis of challenges in constructing datasets for objective memory evaluation, focusing on reliability, diversity, and scalability
Proposed MemSim with BRNet for generating diverse hierarchical user profiles and a causal generation mechanism for constructing reliable QAs
Creation of the MemDaily dataset in daily-life scenarios and a benchmark for evaluating different memory mechanisms of LLM-based agents
methods: The authors introduce MemSim, which first uses a Bayesian Relation Network (BRNet) to model probability distributions over entities and attributes, enabling ancestral sampling to generate diverse hierarchical user profiles without computing intractable joint distributions. Then, a causal generation mechanism constructs informative hints (structured triples) from these profiles and uses LLMs only for rewriting rather than reasoning, producing user messages and five QA types (single-hop, multi-hop, comparative, aggregative, post-processing) along with noise infusion to simulate real-world conditions. Ground truths are derived directly from the structural hints rather than from LLM generation, ensuring reliability.
results: Vanilla LLM-generated ground truth correctness was found to be less than 90% in most scenarios and can fall below 40% in complex scenarios (e.g., aggregative questions like 'How many people are under age 35?'). The MemSim framework was used to create the MemDaily dataset, and extensive experiments were conducted to assess its quality. A benchmark evaluating different memory mechanisms was constructed, though specific numerical results from Section 5 are not included in the provided text.
limitations: The approach depends on a predefined causal structure in BRNet, which may need scenario-specific customization. LLM hallucinations remain a concern when generating confusing choices for multiple-choice questions.
